mappings.note: Why people dance folk dances -- to shed the day's fatigue and amuse themselves, from the extract. Rejected LO-106: the item asks the purpose of the form, not appreciation of folk material.
What folk dance is for -- the dancers' own satisfaction. Rejected LO-106 on the same ground.
Whose question he is answering (Tanushree) -- the item turns on the interview's question-and-answer structure. Rejected LO-107: the dance content is asked in its own items.
Whose presentation he altered (Kathak's) -- about the form. Rejected LO-105: the art, not the man.
What new things he brought into Kathak -- his elders' manner of standing. Rejected LO-105: an addition to the form.
Which tradition he kept and what he changed -- the old tradition kept, the presentation changed. Rejected LO-105: about the art.
What he had noticed -- that his elders' very way of standing was distinctive. Rejected LO-107, kept for items about the form rather than a remembered observation.
The family's finances after his father's death -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-101: a family circumstance, not a local issue to reason about.
Who helped most in the years of struggle (his mother). Rejected LO-100: the item asks who, not about women's position.
What they did with the old zari saris -- burnt them for the gold and silver thread. Rejected LO-101: a household expedient, not an issue.
What the family were once called and what stood at their haveli -- two located details. Rejected LO-107: family history, not the art.
What the now-empty boxes once held -- necklaces worth lakhs, from the extract. Rejected LO-108: no word is glossed.
Whom he entreats (parents) -- the addressee of his argument about children and art. Rejected LO-98: the item asks whom he appeals to, not who questioned him.
What a child should be let play with (lay) -- the technical term put to a new use. Rejected LO-102, kept for the items that state his argument about children.
What he likens dance and music to (a game) -- his claim, which carries his case to parents. Rejected LO-107: the comparison is an argument, not a technical point.

Who asked him what, here -- Shreya's question about a child kept from learning music. The item is about the questioning that drives the interview. Rejected LO-102: the answer he gives is asked in its own item.
What he urges on today's parents -- let the child learn if the interest is there. Rejected LO-98: this is his answer, not the question put to him.
Which dance style he is tied to (Kathak) -- the form. Rejected LO-105: the art, not a biographical fact.
Where his performances are given (in India and abroad) -- a located fact. Rejected LO-107: about his career.
Whose name comes to mind at any mention of Kathak -- located in the introduction. Rejected LO-107: the item asks the name.
Which dance style the passage concerns and who is famously tied to it -- the key adds that Kathak is a North Indian classical form. Rejected LO-105: the form carries the answer.
What is said of his life -- that it rose and fell like the ragas of classical music. The item turns on that simile. Rejected LO-105: the sentence's force is figurative.
What his uncle said about taking a job -- a quoted remark. Rejected LO-102, kept for what he resolved in answer to it.
In which texts Kathak's tradition is traced (Mahabharata and Ramayana) -- the form's antiquity. Rejected LO-105: about the art.
Where the Lucknow gharana's kathiks came from (Hariya village) -- a located fact. Rejected LO-106: the place, not its folk story.
What he resolved in order to become 'Maharaj' -- his answer to his uncle's warning, a position he takes. Rejected LO-105: the resolve is reasoned, not simply stated.
Kathak's early form and where it was confined -- story-telling in temples. Rejected LO-105: the form's history.
Who his gurus were -- three named teachers. Rejected LO-107: names, not the art.
What sort of bond the ganda was (one of sanctity) -- the meaning of a custom of the art. Rejected LO-105: the custom carries it.

What he changed in Kathak (the presentation) -- about the form. Rejected LO-105: the art.
What his uncles and father were to him (keyed 'bhagwan') -- a located relation. Rejected LO-102: no reasoning asked.

Whose poems he drew on for Kathak pieces -- the repertoire he built for the form. Rejected LO-105: about the art. NOTE: the stored key reads 'bhagwan', which is the answer to the preceding item about his uncles and father, so this item's key has bled from its neighbour and is wrong.
What he kept and what he changed in Kathak -- classicism and dignity kept, his own innovation added, complexities eased for a wider public. Rejected LO-105: about the form.
What he learnt from his uncles and father -- lay and taal from one, the faces of abhinaya and the styles from the others. Rejected LO-105: the substance is the art's own content.
